text: The accused stabbed the deceased with a knife after a quarrel over land.
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that there was no intention to kill.
We hold that the injury was sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death, so the offence of murder under Section 302 IPC is made out.
The appeal is dismissed and the conviction under Section 302 IPC is upheld.
relevant_statutes: Section 302 in The Indian Penal Code, 1860

text: The husband and his mother demanded dowry; the wife died of burns within four years of marriage.
The presumption of dowry death under Section 304B IPC applies; cruelty under Section 498A IPC is proved.
Bail is refused.
relevant_statutes: Section 304B in The Indian Penal Code, 1860
Section 498A in The Indian Penal Code, 1860

text: The accused threatened the complainant with dire consequences and showed a knife.
Criminal intimidation under Section 506 IPC is established on the evidence.
The revision petition is dismissed.
relevant_statutes: Section 506 in The Indian Penal Code, 1860

text: Three accused attacked the victim with sticks and a knife in furtherance of a common plan.
Common intention under Section 34 IPC is inferred; the knife injury makes it attempt to murder under Section 307 IPC.
Conviction under Section 307 read with Section 34 IPC is affirmed.
relevant_statutes: Section 307 in The Indian Penal Code, 1860
Section 34 in The Indian Penal Code, 1860

text: The applicant feared arrest in a matrimonial dispute alleging cruelty.
Anticipatory bail under Section 438 CrPC may be granted where the allegations are general; personal liberty under Article 21 weighs heavily.
Anticipatory bail is granted.
relevant_statutes: Section 438 in The Code Of Criminal Procedure, 1973
Section 498A in The Indian Penal Code, 1860

text: The deceased was stabbed repeatedly with a knife during a robbery.
In our view the multiple knife injuries show intention to cause death; murder under Section 302 IPC.
The appeal is dismissed.
relevant_statutes: Section 302 in The Indian Penal Code, 1860

text: Whether bail can be refused solely because the offence is serious.
It is well settled that personal liberty under Article 21 cannot be curtailed except by fair procedure; bail is the rule.
The petition is allowed and bail is granted.
relevant_statutes: Section 438 in The Code Of Criminal Procedure, 1973

text: The wife alleged harassment for dowry and cruelty by her husband's relatives.
Cruelty under Section 498A IPC is made out against the husband only; general allegations against relatives fail.
The petition is partly allowed.
relevant_statutes: Section 498A in The Indian Penal Code, 1860
